issues.description: Operator precedence in `not key == Qt.Key_Tab` is correct but unreadable; rewrite as `key != Qt.Key_Tab`.
issues.detail: Python parses this as `not (key == Qt.Key_Tab)`, which happens to be intended. But a reader must pause to verify that, instead of reading `key != Qt.Key_Tab` at a glance. Code in a keyPressEvent handler is exactly the place where a reader cannot afford ambiguity. NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT.

issues.description: The new guard fires for every key, not just Enter/Return; the invariant is unstated and likely wrong.
issues.detail: The branch lives inside the Enter/Return handler block, but the added condition only excludes Tab. If control reaches this code for any non-Tab key while the setting is off, it hides the popup and forwards the event. The intended invariant -- 'when Enter is disabled, treat Enter like a normal keystroke' -- needs to be stated and the guard narrowed to Return/Enter keys explicitly. UNDER-AUDITED.

issues.description: `get_conf` called on every keypress inside the completion popup; cache or read once.
issues.detail: Reading a config value through the plugin conf system on every key event is wasteful in a hot path (the popup's keyPressEvent). A literate version would read the setting once at popup show, store it on self, and consult the attribute here. Not a profiler-confirmed hot spot, so flag as a small cleanup, not a P0. ASYMPTOTICALLY-OK-PRACTICALLY-SLOW.

issues.description: No literate comment explains why the popup hides and re-dispatches the event.
issues.detail: The three-line block silently changes a non-obvious behavior: dismiss the popup, then replay the keystroke into the editor so Enter inserts a newline instead of accepting. A one-line comment stating the invariant ('Enter-acceptance disabled: forward Enter to the editor as a normal newline') would make this code readable without running it. NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT.

issues.description: Config key default `True` is correct, but no migration note for existing users.
issues.detail: Adding `use_enter_for_completions: True` to defaults preserves prior behavior, which is right. Confirm the config versioning bump (CONF_VERSION) is handled elsewhere; otherwise users on existing configs will not get the new key until reset. Low risk but worth a one-line audit. RIGOROUS-pending-verification.

review.summary: Small, well-scoped change with a correct-by-default config flag. The algorithmic content is trivial -- one branch in a keyPressEvent -- but the branch is written in a way that obscures its invariant: `not key == Qt.Key_Tab` should be `key != Qt.Key_Tab`, and the guard is placed inside the Enter-handler block without restating that it only applies to Enter/Return. A one-line literate comment plus narrowing the key check would make this RIGOROUS instead of UNDER-AUDITED. Reading `get_conf` on every keystroke is a minor practical-constants issue, not a complexity issue. Verdict: UNDER-AUDITED, fixable with a small rewrite.
